question.text: You are the Compliance Officer of 'Vindhya Long-Short Fund' (Cat III open-ended AIF). In one week, the fund has: (a) a foreign investor group whose UBO traces to a land-border country and that contributes at least 50% of the fund's corpus; (b) a Cat I FPI seeking AI status for LVF subscription; (c) a breach of the 2x leverage cap on a particular day; and (d) a delay in filing the FLA return. Which of the following sequences is the CORRECT regulatory response?

answer.text: Ignore the leverage breach if intraday; file FLA annually by 15th July; AI status is automatic for any FPI; UBO screen is optional
Suspend the fund immediately for all four issues and seek SEBI permission before continuing operations
Resign as Compliance Officer to avoid personal liability

(a) Conduct specific due diligence on the land-border-UBO investor group because the 50%-of-corpus threshold is triggered; (b) treat the Cat I FPI as a deemed Accredited Investor, no separate AI certificate, but document the FPI certificate and obtain an AI consent undertaking for LVF; (c) report the leverage breach to the Custodian immediately, intimate investors before 10 AM the next working day, square off the excess by EOD the next working day and send confirmation, with the Custodian reporting to SEBI before 10 AM the next working day; (d) file the FLA return on FLAIR by 15 July, with the delay recorded and disclosed

explanation.text: The Logic: Each limb maps to a specific compliance obligation. Land-border specific due diligence is triggered where the relevant investor group meets the 50% corpus/UBO threshold, so the stem is now framed accordingly. A Cat I FPI is treated as a deemed Accredited Investor under the AI framework, but LVF subscription still requires an AI consent undertaking on record. The 2x leverage breach for Cat III AIFs follows the prescribed breach-reporting and square-off timelines through the Custodian to SEBI. FLA filing on the FLAIR portal is due by 15 July each year, with any delay recorded in the compliance file. The Trap: Option A under-reacts on each limb (ignoring the breach, treating AI as automatic for any FPI, skipping the UBO screen). Option B over-reacts by suspending the fund and seeking blanket SEBI permission rather than following the prescribed remediation path. Option C abandons the role of Compliance Officer, which is itself problematic from a fit-and-proper standpoint. Note: Treat this as a synthesis check across four streams: land-border specific due diligence at the 50% corpus/UBO threshold; deemed AI status for Cat I FPIs with LVF consent documentation; the leverage breach reporting and square-off chain through the Custodian; and the 15 July FLA filing on FLAIR with delay recorded.
